title: ‘Self-proclaimed journalists may not get same protection as accredited ones’: SC on anti-CEC protest pleas

ai.summary: The Supreme Court noted that self-proclaimed journalists may not receive the same protection as accredited reporters during anti-CEC protests, stating that journalist status is not self-conferred and must be accredited through official channels.

facts.claim: Self-proclaimed journalists may not enjoy the same protection which is given to accredited reporters
facts.quote: Self-proclaimed journalists may not enjoy the same protection which is given to accredited reporters, the Supreme Court noted on Thursday while hearing pleas over ill-treatment of media personnel during anti-CEC protests in Delhi.

facts.claim: Status as a journalist is not self-conferred
facts.quote: The top court, in context of the pleas, noted that the status as a journalist “is not self-conferred,” adding that reporters are accredited according to their medium.

facts.claim: Reporters are accredited according to their medium
facts.quote: If you're a journalist from a newspaper/print media, you're under [Press Council] accredited journalist...if you are a TV channel of that newspaper you are accredited accordingly...you can also be an online journalist and you can also have registration.

ai.background_note: The Supreme Court is addressing the definition of journalists and their protection during protests following complaints of police misconduct against media personnel during anti-CEC demonstrations in Delhi.
